authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Grew 1.5x Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: The 1970s food shortage warnings missed how quickly cereal production grew.
says: From 1985 to 2017, progression to secondary school rose from 77.8% to 91.3% — 1.2 times higher.
From 1972 to 2024, cereal production rose from 1083.7 to 1644.1 million metric tons — 1.5 times higher.
Farmland spans 5.2 million square kilometers in China, 4.2 in the United States, 3.6 Australia, 2.4 Brazil, and 2.2 Russia.
authored_explainer.closing: Food production changed faster than the old shortage warnings expected.
authored_explainer.question: Which surprised you most: school, grain, or land?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible Renewables And Waste Tripled 3.0x Since 1990
authored_explainer.hook: Since 1990, waste tripled as an energy source—not solar or wind.
says: From 1990 to 2024, combustible renewables and waste rose from 10.2% to 30.1% of energy — 3.0 times higher.
From 1998 to 2024, electricity access rose from 73.2% to 91.9% of population — 1.3 times higher.
From 1972 to 2024, methane (CH4) emissions from waste rose from 903.8 to 1,652 Mt CO2e — 1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: Waste now supplies far more energy, while its methane cost keeps climbing.
authored_explainer.question: Which surprised you most: fuel, power, or waste?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth slowed while cities kept expanding.
says: From 1972 to 2025, rural population fell from 63.1% to 42.2% of total population — down to 67 percent.
From 1972 to 2025, the largest city's share shifted from 18.2% to 16.2% of urban population — barely moved.
From 1972 to 2025, population growth fell from 2 annual % to 0.91 annual % — down to 46 percent.
authored_explainer.closing: The population still grows, but the annual pace is now less than half as fast.
authored_explainer.question: Which surprised you most: rural, city, or growth?

authored_explainer.title: Pol3 Immunization Grew 4.6x Since 1980
authored_explainer.hook: In 1980 it was 18.3; now it's 84.2, a reversal hiding in plain sight.
says: From 1972 to 2024, the rate fell from 11.7 to 7.55 per 1,000 people — down to 65 percent.
From 2000 to 2019, it fell from 48.9 to 40.5 — down to 83 percent.
From 1980 to 2024, Pol3 immunization rose from 18.3 to 84.2 — 4.6 times higher.
From 1985 to 2023, the count fell from 625,000 to 260,000 — down to 42 percent.
authored_explainer.closing: Pol3 immunization rose dramatically while every companion measure moved the other way.
authored_explainer.question: Which reversal surprised you most?

authored_explainer.title: Air Passengers Grew 10.6x Since 1973
authored_explainer.hook: In 1973, 401.6 million became 4269.0 million—air travel scaled beyond recognition.
says: From 1973 to 2023, air passengers climbed from 401.6 million to 4269.0 million — 10.6 times higher.
China leads at 946,499 million passenger-km; Korea, Rep. follows at 100,381 million passenger-km.
From 2010 to 2024, passenger volume rose from 547.1 million to 913.3 million — 1.7 times higher.
From 1995 to 2019, the export share fell from 8.54% to 7.39% — down to 87 percent.
authored_explainer.closing: Air travel became mass movement, while its economic share did not rise with it.
authored_explainer.question: Which air-travel number surprised you?

authored_explainer.title: Urban Open Defecation Fell 87% Since 2000
says: From 1972 to 2025, ages 15-64 grew from 2191.8 million to 5355.5 million — 2.4 times higher.
Russian Federation spans 17.1 million sq. km; Brazil spans 8.5 million sq. km.
From 2000 to 2024, urban open defecation fell from 5.14% to 0.69% — down to 13 percent.
From 2010 to 2025, forcibly displaced people rose from 41.1 million to 117.3 million — 2.9 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: Sanitation advanced sharply, even as displacement shows how uneven human security remains.
authored_explainer.question: Which human-security shift surprised you?

authored_explainer.title: Ukraine's Battle-Death Toll Leads By 6.7x
authored_explainer.hook: Sri Lanka had 10,165; Ukraine reached 68,097, putting the scale beyond comparison.
says: From 2000 to 2023, homicides fell from 6.85 to 5.2 per 100,000 people — down to 76 percent.
Ukraine leads at 68,097 battle-related deaths; Russian Federation records 7,670.
Greece leads at 23,795 heating degree days; Iceland records 11,456.
authored_explainer.closing: Battle deaths dwarf the other rankings, showing how war reshapes every national comparison.
authored_explainer.question: Which comparison changed your perspective?
